previous_versions.body: Actually you do •not• need encoding, injection or sanitization for the most severe form of injection. You need query parameterization to stop SQL injection.This is why injection is a lot more difficult to fix than most people think because each individual type of injection has a very different formula for how it needs to be fixed.

Also, there are many ASVS items that can be grouped into one ASVS item under the name of input validation (all injection related attaks) but we have not done that (which is good).

A bit offtopic, but - against injection attack you need mostly encoding, then sanitization, then input validation.

The point here is to make the tester aware of this attack vector.

Yes, awareness is good. The question - is ASVS the correct project to achieve it (if the reason is only awareness)?
And back to the beginning: can you provide an example - how loop bound injection can happen if input validation (including JSON schema validation) is done correctly?
Where I want to reach is - if it's not a separate and independent problem, then I'm not sure it's worth separate and independent requirement. Note: I'm not sure does not mean I'm against that.
